Elara Dawn — Album 8.5: Elara Dawn

The Lighted of the South

"The Lighted of the South"

[Intro — the sight takes her south, to something quieter than anything she’s seen] She expected armies She expected the battlefield she came from

The sight takes her south And shows her a kitchen

[Verse 1 — ordinary people, ordinary days] There is a woman grinding grain

There is a man repairing a wheel

There are children arguing about something the way children argue about things that are everything when you are small enough for everything to be close

There is a fire There is soup There is someone singing off-key and happy about it

And there is something else

Something underneath all of it Like a second heartbeat You would not notice unless you were listening for it

[Pre-Chorus] She listens

And she hears it

It is not magic It is not power It is not the gaze or the lightning or the weight of 300,000 years moving through a body in a tower

It is just

truth

Being held

By people who decided to keep holding it

[Chorus] The Lighted of the South Are not what the church described The Lighted of the South Are not the ones who emptied villages overnight They are the woman grinding grain They are the man repairing the wheel They are the ones who move When the raids come And set up somewhere new And light the fire again And grind the grain again And keep the truth in the ordinary things where no one thinks to look for it

The Lighted of the South Have been doing this For two hundred and ninety thousand years

[Verse 2 — the raids, the moving, the holding on] She sees them move

She has seen armies move She has seen companies ride south She has seen the church mark the map and send the blade

She has never watched the ones the blade was sent for

Pack a child on each hip Take what fits in one bag Leave the fire Leave the grain Leave the things that don’t survive the running

And find a new place south of the last place And light a new fire And grind the grain again And say: This is the truth This is what we carry This is why we move instead of stop

[Pre-Chorus 2] She sees a man Who does not know why he carries what he carries

He only knows his mother gave it to him And her mother gave it to her And somewhere back further than memory goes someone decided: this is worth the cost of holding

And held

[Chorus] The Lighted of the South Are not what the church described The Lighted of the South Are not the ones who emptied villages overnight They are the woman grinding grain They are the man repairing the wheel They are the ones who move When the raids come And set up somewhere new And light the fire again And grind the grain again And keep the truth in the ordinary things where no one thinks to look for it

The Lighted of the South Have been doing this For two hundred and ninety thousand years

[Bridge — Elara understanding what she was always supposed to be] She was built to be a sword

She knows that now

She was built to be the weapon the church aimed at the castle at the purple woman at the thing they called the dark

She was not built for this She was not built for the woman grinding grain She was not built for the man with the wheel She was not built for the children who argue about small things because the world is still small enough for small things to matter

She was not built for this

But this This is what needed protecting

Not the church Not the doctrine Not the border on the map Not the trade routes Not the light the council wanted pointed in a specific direction

This

The fire The grain The singing off-key The moving south again when the raids come

The truth held by ordinary hands for two hundred and ninety thousand years without an army without a miracle without a chosen one

Just people who decided: this is worth it

Just people who kept deciding every generation every raid every burned camp every bag they packed in the dark

worth it worth it worth it

[Pre-Chorus 3 — she stands] She is still in the cosmic field

She has been on her knees since T7

She stands up

Not because she is ready

Because they were not ready either

And they held anyway

[Final Chorus] The Lighted of the South I see you now The Lighted of the South I understand now what I was always supposed to do

Not the sword the church sharpened Not the weapon aimed at the wrong woman Not the chosen one who never chose

The light that walks toward the fire and says: I will not let this go out

Not in my time Not while I am standing

The Lighted of the South Have held this door open For two hundred and ninety thousand years

I will hold it For whatever time I have left

[Outro — Elara’s vow, quiet and certain] She does not say it to the church She does not say it to the Order She does not say it to the light or the mission or the name they gave her

She says it to the woman with the grain She says it to the man with the wheel She says it to the children who are still arguing about something small

I see you

I have always been yours

I just did not know it until now
